 Bangladesh's fourth or Pakistan's first? A blockbuster 'final' beckons
 Published : 14 November 2026
 • 
 Updated : 14 November 2026, 14:34
 • 
 FOOTBALL
 SHARE 
 Sports Reporter 
 Balancing act! Bangladesh's 19-year-old 'Wonderboy' Farhaan Ali Wahid cushions the ball on his head as Hamza Choudhury, Jamal Bhuyan, Tariq Kazi, and Bishwanath Ghosh watch on during training in Dhaka yesterday. Fresh off a dazzling solo goal in the 4-0 rout of Sri Lanka, the electric left-winger will be out to weave more of that same magic against Pakistan in the SAFF Championship semifinal today as Bangladesh chase a fourth final. [R] Pakistan players in action during training. Photo: Firoz Ahmed / PFF 
 Former champions Bangladesh stand one win away from their first SAFF Championship final since 2005, but a resurgent Pakistan, strengthened by an influx of European-based players, stand in their way when the two sides meet in Saturday's second semifinal at the National Stadium. 
 The match kicks off at 8:30pm, following the first semifinal between holders India and dark horses Bhutan at 3:00pm.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 For Bangladesh, it is a chance to end a 21-year wait for a final appearance and move within one win of a second regional title following their only triumph, which came on home soil in 2003, and six group-stage exits in the last eight editions.
 This time, however, Thomas Dooley's side have given supporters reason to dream. Backed by overseas-based players, including Sheffield United midfielder Hamza Choudhury, Bangladesh topped Group A, scoring five goals and conceding none. Their emphatic 4-0 win over Sri Lanka on Wednesday, following an earlier victory over Bhutan, has given them all the necessary momentum before a fixture which the Bangladesh head coach has labelled “the final”.
 Read more A perfect 10, but the best is yet to come 
 Pakistan, meanwhile, have made an uneven but encouraging start under coach Nolberto Solano. They pushed defending champions India close in a 3-2 defeat after trailing 3-0, then bounced back with a 3-0 win over former champions Maldives. Their resilience was also evident in September, when they came from two goals down to draw 2-2 with a higher-ranked Philippines side in the FIFA ASEAN Cup.
 Their campaign has been shaped by the late arrival of five overseas-based regulars -- Abdullah Iqbal, Easah Suliman, Adil Nabi, Abdul Samad Arshad and Ali Akbar Khan -- who missed the group stage because it fell outside the FIFA international window.
 Sweden-based Iqbal and former England youth international Suliman, who plays in Azerbaijan, strengthen the backline alongside Iqbal, while Nabi, a West Bromwich Albion academy product who plies his trade in Greece, adds creativity in midfield. Denmark-based Abdul Samad offers another attacking option, with six-foot-two Ali Akbar providing a further presence up front. How quickly the newly arrived players can settle into the side, however, remains a question.
 Read more ‘Don’t care about Hamza’: Pakistan captain backs their ‘amazing’ diaspora players for SAFF semi 
 Pakistan's push for a maiden title comes against a difficult domestic backdrop, having been devoid of top-tier action since the 2018-19 season and faced multiple FIFA suspensions since 2017, the latest of which was lifted in March last year.
 They have struggled to make the final despite reaching the semifinals on several occasions. Maldives and Bangladesh eliminated them in 2003 and 2005 respectively, while India knocked them out in 1997 and 2018. They have reached the last four in Dhaka on three of their previous four visits, but this will be their first semifinal against hosts Bangladesh.
 In their last 10 encounters spanning three decades, Bangladesh won four times, drew five and lost once. Bangladesh won 1-0 in 2018, the last time the two teams met. Dooley, however, is well aware of the quality Pakistan's reinforcements bring. "They [Pakistan] also have incredible football knowledge because they are playing at a higher level in Europe," Dooley told reporters before yesterday's training session at Bashundhara Kings Arena.
 The Bangladesh coach, however, is confident his players can reproduce the intensity they showed against Sri Lanka. "We just have to do the same thing. We have to show the fans that we can play football… and that's what we have to show Pakistan too."
 Bangladesh are expected to retain the balance that served them well against Sri Lanka, with Hamza, Shamit Shome and Quazem Shah - all central to their midfield control and left-forward Farhaan Ali Wahid looking to build on his outstanding solo goal. The hosts will, however, have to adjust their backline following Saad Uddin's injury, which ruled the right-back out of the tournament.
 Read more Arrives the Wonderboy: Why Farhaan’s golazo changes everything for Bangladesh 
 The introduction of Video Assistant Referee (VAR) for the knockout rounds adds another dimension to a contest that promises to be physical and closely fought. With Bangladesh seeking a return to the final and Pakistan chasing a historic first under the glare of the Dhaka floodlights, the stage is set for a “final” before the final, where desperation, diaspora ambition and tactical moves collide. 
 Obviously if you are more rested it helps. But this game is, for us, a final because I think Pakistan are one of the best teams.
 Thomas Dooley, Bangladesh coach
